chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who says to his wife, 'You are free from me,' or 'disavowed,' or 'severed,' or 'prohibited.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not with anything.'

key_terms.خَلِيَّةٌ: Free, released, or exempt (from the marital bond)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ: It is not with anything (i.e., not a specific formal act like talaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband tells his wife she is 'free' or 'disavowed' from him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that casual declarations of separation using phrases like 'khalīyah' (free) or 'barī’ah' (disavowed) do not constitute a formal, binding divorce (*talaq*) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing them from explicit legal utterances. This ruling underscores the principle of *iḥtirām al-zhāhir* (respect for the apparent meaning) while requiring specific intent (*niyyah*) for legal acts, a key distinction in Usuli scholarship. It highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in preventing hasty divorces by requiring clear, intentional language rather than colloquial expressions of displeasure.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the man who is saying to his wife, ‘You are, from me, free’, or ‘disavowed’, or ‘severed’, or ‘prohibited’’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says to his wife, ’You from my side are free, cleared and severed’ or ‘you are unlawful.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect.’”
